meta.description: Batch interest calculation program that computes and posts monthly interest charges and fees to credit card accounts based on transaction category balances and account-specific interest rates.
meta.process_description: The program reads transaction category balance records sequentially, grouping them by account. For each account, it retrieves the account master data and the card-to-account cross-reference, then looks up the applicable interest rate from a discount/rate group table based on the account's group classification and the transaction type and category. Where a non-zero interest rate applies, it calculates the interest amount for that transaction category balance and any associated fees, accumulating totals at the account level. When all categories for an account have been processed, it writes the computed interest and fees back to the account master file and generates corresponding transaction records to create an auditable trail of the interest charges applied.

files.TCATBAL-FILE: Transaction Category Balance file – holds the outstanding balance for each account broken down by transaction type and category, serving as the basis for interest calculation
files.XREF-FILE: Card-to-Account Cross-Reference file – maps credit card numbers to customer and account identifiers, used to resolve account context
files.DISCGRP-FILE: Discount/Interest Rate Group file – holds the applicable interest rates keyed by account group, transaction type, and transaction category
files.ACCOUNT-FILE: Account Master file – stores core account data including credit limits, current balances, and account group classification; updated with computed interest charges
files.TRANSACT-FILE: Transaction output file – receives newly generated interest charge and fee transaction records for audit and downstream processing

business_rules: Interest is calculated at the transaction category level: each combination of account, transaction type, and transaction category may carry a different interest rate.
Interest is only computed and fees only assessed when the applicable interest rate for that category is non-zero; zero-rate categories are skipped entirely.

Interest rates are determined by the account's assigned group (ACCT-GROUP-ID) combined with the transaction type code and transaction category code, allowing differentiated pricing across customer segments and spend categories.

Account balances are updated in batch at the end of processing each account's categories, ensuring all category-level interest amounts are accumulated before a single account master write is performed.
Each interest or fee charge generates a discrete transaction record, providing a complete audit trail of all system-generated charges.
The program accepts a processing date as an external parameter, enabling it to be run for specific statement or billing cycle dates rather than always using the current system date.
The card-to-account cross-reference must be resolved for every account processed, ensuring interest postings are correctly associated with the right account even when initiated from card-level data.
A sequential suffix counter ensures uniqueness of generated transaction IDs within a single batch run, preventing duplicate transaction records.

This paragraph calculates the monthly interest charge for a single transaction category balance by applying the category-specific annual interest rate, then accumulates the result into the account-level interest total and records the charge as an auditable transaction.
Begins the interest calculation formula for the current transaction category balance.
Divides the product of the outstanding category balance and the applicable annual interest rate by 1200 to derive the monthly interest charge (converting an annual rate to a monthly fraction).
Adds the newly computed monthly interest charge for this category to the running total of all interest charges accumulated so far for the current account.
Triggers the sub-process that writes a discrete transaction record to the output file, creating an auditable record of this specific interest charge.
Marks the end of this paragraph and returns control to the calling routine.

Closes the transaction ID construction step.
Classifies the transaction as a standard purchase/charge type (code '01'), identifying this system-generated entry as a regular debit charge to the account.
Assigns the transaction to category '05', which designates this charge specifically as an interest assessment within the bank's transaction categorisation scheme.
Marks the originating source of this transaction as 'System', distinguishing it from customer-initiated or merchant-initiated transactions and flagging it as a batch-generated charge.
Begins building the human-readable transaction description by prefixing it with 'Int. for a/c' to clearly label this as an interest charge...
...appended with the account number, so that the description unambiguously identifies which credit card account the interest is being charged to.

Places the completed descriptive label into the transaction record's description field for display on statements and audit reports.

Records the calculated monthly interest amount for this transaction category as the monetary value of the charge being posted to the account.
Sets the merchant identifier to zero, indicating this is not a purchase from an external merchant but a bank-originated system charge.

Clears the merchant city field, as no physical or online merchant location is associated with an interest charge.
Clears the merchant postal code field, consistent with this being a bank-generated fee rather than a point-of-sale transaction.
Associates the interest charge transaction with the credit card number linked to this account, ensuring the charge appears correctly on the cardholder's card-level statement.

Sets a recognised system-level failure code (999) that will be reported to the job scheduler and operations monitoring tools, uniquely identifying this as a critical batch abend.

Invokes the IBM Language Environment abnormal termination service to forcibly halt the batch job, propagating the failure code and timing instruction so the job scheduler records the run as failed and triggers any configured alerts or restart procedures.
Entry point for the file error reporting routine, invoked whenever a file operation returns an unexpected result during batch processing.
Checks whether the file error code is in an abnormal or non-standard format, indicating a system-level or hardware-related file failure rather than a standard application-level error.
Also catches errors beginning with '9', which signal serious operating-system or file-system level failures that require special formatting to display correctly.
Captures the first character of the error code — representing the primary error category — into the first position of the four-digit display field.
Clears a temporary numeric work area to zero, preparing it to receive and convert the secondary error detail byte into a displayable number.
Places the secondary error detail byte — which encodes additional failure specifics in binary form — into the low-order position of the temporary conversion area.
Converts the binary-encoded secondary error detail into a standard numeric value so it can be displayed alongside the primary error category in a readable format.
Prints the fully formatted four-digit file error code to the job log, giving operations staff the exact failure code needed to diagnose the file problem.
Begins the handling path for standard, numeric file status codes that follow the conventional two-digit file status format.
Initialises the four-digit display field to zeros, ensuring no residual data from a previous error contaminates the current error message.
Inserts the standard two-digit file status code into the last two positions of the four-digit display field, right-aligning it for consistent presentation.
Prints the formatted standard file error code to the job log so operations staff can identify the exact nature of the file access failure.
Closes the conditional logic that distinguishes between system-level and standard file errors.
Returns control to the calling routine after the error code has been displayed, allowing the program to continue its error-handling or termination sequence.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD
variables.description: File buffer record for the Transaction Category Balance file. Represents one line of the outstanding balance breakdown per account, transaction type, and category — the raw input data that drives interest calculation for each billing segment.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY
variables.description: Composite lookup key for a transaction category balance record, combining the account identifier, transaction type, and category code to uniquely identify which balance segment is being processed for interest calculation.

variables.name: FD-TRANCAT-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The credit card account number associated with this balance segment. Identifies which customer account owns the outstanding balance being read from the Transaction Category Balance file, used to group and accumulate interest charges per account.

variables.name: FD-TRANCAT-TYPE-CD
variables.description: The transaction type code (e.g., purchase, cash advance) for this balance segment. Together with the category code, it determines which interest rate tier applies to this portion of the account's outstanding balance.

variables.name: FD-TRANCAT-CD
variables.description: The transaction category code (e.g., groceries, travel, fuel) for this balance segment. Combined with the transaction type and account group, it drives the lookup of the specific interest rate applicable to this spending category.

variables.name: FD-FD-TRAN-CAT-DATA
variables.description: The remaining data portion of the transaction category balance record beyond the key fields, including the actual outstanding balance amount for this category. This balance is the principal figure on which monthly interest is computed.

variables.name: FD-XREFFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the Card-to-Account Cross-Reference file. Represents the mapping between a physical credit card number and the underlying customer and account identifiers, used to ensure interest charges are posted to the correct account.

variables.name: FD-XREF-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number as it appears on the physical card. Serves as the lookup key into the cross-reference file to resolve which account and customer this card belongs to before posting interest charges.

variables.name: FD-XREF-CUST-NUM
variables.description: The unique customer identifier linked to this credit card. Identifies the individual cardholder associated with the account, providing the customer context needed for correct interest posting and audit trail.

variables.name: FD-XREF-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The account number resolved from the card cross-reference. This is the target account to which interest charges will be posted, ensuring that card-level transaction data is correctly associated with the right account master record.

variables.name: FD-XREF-FILLER
variables.description: Unused padding bytes in the cross-reference file record to meet the fixed record length of 50 bytes. Carries no business meaning but ensures correct file I/O alignment.

variables.name: FD-DISCGRP-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the Discount/Interest Rate Group file. Represents one interest rate rule entry, defining what rate applies to a specific combination of account group, transaction type, and transaction category — the core pricing table for interest calculation.

variables.name: FD-DISCGRP-KEY
variables.description: Composite key used to look up the applicable interest rate for a given account segment. Combines the account group classification, transaction type, and transaction category to pinpoint the exact rate tier that should be applied.

variables.name: FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID
variables.description: The account group classification used as the first dimension of the interest rate lookup. Different customer segments (e.g., premium, standard, secured) are assigned different group IDs, enabling differentiated interest rate pricing across the portfolio.

variables.name: FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD
variables.description: The transaction type code dimension of the interest rate lookup key. Allows the bank to charge different rates for different types of transactions (e.g., a higher rate for cash advances versus regular purchases) within the same account group.

variables.name: FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD
variables.description: The transaction category code dimension of the interest rate lookup key. Enables category-level interest rate differentiation (e.g., promotional 0% rate on balance transfers vs. standard rate on retail purchases) within a given account group and transaction type.

variables.name: FD-DISCGRP-DATA
variables.description: The data payload of the discount group record beyond the key, containing the actual interest rate value for this pricing rule. This rate is the percentage applied to the category balance to compute the monthly interest charge.

variables.name: FD-ACCTFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the Account Master file. Represents a single customer account record containing credit limits, current balances, and account classification — the record that is read to obtain account group for rate lookup and updated with computed interest charges.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique account identifier in the Account Master file. Used to locate the correct account record for reading the account group classification and subsequently updating the account balance with the total interest charges computed for the billing cycle.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The remaining account master data beyond the account ID, including current balance, credit limits, account group, and other account attributes. This data is mapped to the ACCOUNT-RECORD copybook structure for processing and is rewritten after interest charges are added to the account balance.

variables.name: FD-TRANFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the Transaction output file. Represents a newly generated interest charge or fee transaction record that will be written to the transaction file, creating an auditable record of every system-generated interest posting for the billing cycle.

variables.name: FD-TRANS-ID
variables.description: The unique transaction identifier for the generated interest or fee transaction. Ensures each interest posting can be individually tracked, reconciled, and audited in downstream systems and statements.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The remaining transaction record data beyond the transaction ID, including transaction type, category, amount, merchant details, card number, and timestamps. This payload is mapped from the TRAN-RECORD copybook and constitutes the full detail of the interest charge being recorded.

variables.name: TCATBALF-STATUS
variables.description: I/O status indicator for the Transaction Category Balance file. After every file operation (open, read, close), this two-character code is checked to confirm the operation succeeded or to identify the specific error, ensuring the program does not silently process corrupt or missing balance data.

variables.name: TCATBALF-STAT1
variables.description: The primary status character for the Transaction Category Balance file I/O operation. A value of '0' indicates success; any other value signals a file error that must be investigated to prevent incorrect interest calculations.

variables.name: TCATBALF-STAT2
variables.description: The secondary status character for the Transaction Category Balance file, providing additional detail about the I/O result (e.g., end-of-file condition vs. a hard error). Used together with TCATBALF-STAT1 to fully diagnose file processing issues.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STATUS
variables.description: I/O status indicator for the Card-to-Account Cross-Reference file. Checked after each file operation to confirm that card-to-account resolution succeeded, preventing interest charges from being posted to the wrong account due to a file access failure.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The primary status character for the Cross-Reference file I/O operation. Indicates whether the card-to-account lookup succeeded, allowing the program to detect and handle cases where a card number cannot be resolved to an account.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The secondary status character for the Cross-Reference file, providing granular error detail to distinguish between a record-not-found condition and a more serious file system error during account resolution.

variables.name: DISCGRP-STATUS
variables.description: I/O status indicator for the Discount/Interest Rate Group file. Checked after each rate lookup to confirm that the applicable interest rate was successfully retrieved, ensuring no interest is calculated using a stale or missing rate.

variables.name: DISCGRP-STAT1
variables.description: The primary status character for the Discount Group file I/O operation. A successful read confirms that a valid interest rate was found for the account group, transaction type, and category combination being processed.

variables.name: DISCGRP-STAT2
variables.description: The secondary status character for the Discount Group file, providing additional diagnostic detail when a rate lookup fails, such as distinguishing a missing rate record from a file access error.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STATUS
variables.description: I/O status indicator for the Account Master file. Checked after every read and rewrite operation to confirm that account data was successfully retrieved and that interest charges were successfully posted back to the account record.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The primary status character for the Account Master file I/O operation. Critical for confirming that account balance updates containing computed interest charges were written successfully, preventing silent data loss.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The secondary status character for the Account Master file, providing granular error information to distinguish between a record-not-found condition and a write failure when updating account balances with interest charges.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STATUS
variables.description: I/O status indicator for the Transaction output file. Checked after each interest transaction record is written to confirm the audit trail entry was successfully recorded, ensuring no interest posting is applied to an account without a corresponding transaction record.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The primary status character for the Transaction file write operation. Confirms that each generated interest charge transaction was successfully written to the output file for downstream processing and audit.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The secondary status character for the Transaction file, providing additional error detail when a transaction write fails, enabling precise diagnosis of output file issues during the interest posting batch run.

variables.name: IO-STATUS
variables.description: General-purpose I/O status holder used for consolidated error handling and reporting across file operations. Captures the two-character file status code for display in error messages when any file operation fails during the interest calculation batch.

variables.name: IO-STAT1
variables.description: The primary character of the general I/O status code. Used in error reporting routines to communicate the high-level outcome of a failed file operation to operations staff investigating a batch abend.

variables.name: IO-STAT2
variables.description: The secondary character of the general I/O status code. Provides the detailed sub-code needed by operations staff to pinpoint the exact nature of a file error during the interest calculation batch run.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-BINARY
variables.description: A two-byte binary work field used to convert numeric file status codes into their individual character components. Enables the program to split a binary status value into left and right bytes for readable error reporting and diagnostic messaging.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-ALPHA
variables.description: Alphanumeric overlay of the TWO-BYTES-BINARY field. Allows the same two bytes of binary status data to be read as individual characters, enabling human-readable error code extraction for batch job failure diagnostics.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-LEFT
variables.description: The left (high-order) byte of the binary status code when interpreted as text. Corresponds to the primary status character of a file I/O result, used in error message formatting for operations staff.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
variables.description: The right (low-order) byte of the binary status code when interpreted as text. Corresponds to the secondary status character of a file I/O result, providing the detailed sub-code in error messages.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-04
variables.description: Structured breakdown of a four-digit I/O status code into its component parts. Used to decompose and display file status codes in a format suitable for error logging and operator notification when a file operation fails during the batch run.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0401
variables.description: The leading single digit of the four-digit I/O status code, representing the primary status class (e.g., 0=success, 1=end-of-file, 2=invalid key, 9=system error). Initialized to zero and updated during error handling to reflect the actual file operation outcome.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0403
variables.description: The trailing three digits of the four-digit I/O status code, providing the detailed sub-status for error diagnosis. Together with IO-STATUS-0401, forms the complete status code reported to operations when a file error occurs during interest batch processing.

variables.name: APPL-RESULT
variables.description: General application return code used to communicate the outcome of processing steps within the interest calculation program. Drives conditional logic to determine whether processing completed successfully or encountered an error requiring abend or special handling.

variables.name: APPL-AOK
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the last processing step completed successfully (return code = 0). When true, the program continues normal interest calculation processing without error intervention.

variables.name: APPL-EOF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the end of the Transaction Category Balance input file has been reached (return code = 16). When true, the program knows all account balance records have been processed and triggers final account update and batch wrap-up.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the Transaction Category Balance input file has been fully read. Initialized to 'N' (not at end) and set to 'Y' when the last balance record is read, signaling the main processing loop to stop reading and finalize the last account's interest charges.

variables.name: ABCODE
variables.description: Abend code used when the program must terminate abnormally due to an unrecoverable error (e.g., file open failure, unexpected I/O error). The code is passed to the system to identify the reason for the batch job failure in the job log.

variables.name: TIMING
variables.description: Timing or performance measurement field used to capture elapsed processing time or serve as a parameter for system timing calls. Supports operational monitoring of the interest calculation batch job's execution duration.

variables.name: COBOL-TS
variables.description: Timestamp work area used to capture and format the current date and time for stamping generated interest transaction records. Provides the origination and processing timestamps that appear on each interest charge transaction written to the output file.

variables.name: COB-YYYY
variables.description: The four-digit year component of the current processing timestamp. Used to construct the date portion of the timestamp stamped on generated interest transaction records, ensuring transactions are correctly dated for the billing cycle.

variables.name: COB-MM
variables.description: The two-digit month component of the current processing timestamp. Combined with year and day, forms the calendar date recorded on each interest charge transaction to identify the billing period in which the charge was assessed.

variables.name: COB-DD
variables.description: The two-digit day component of the current processing timestamp. Identifies the specific day within the billing month on which the interest charge transaction was generated and posted to the account.

variables.name: COB-HH
variables.description: The two-digit hour component of the current processing timestamp. Provides the time-of-day precision on interest transaction records, supporting intra-day reconciliation and audit of when the batch interest posting run executed.

variables.name: COB-MIN
variables.description: The two-digit minute component of the current processing timestamp. Together with the hour, provides minute-level precision on the timestamp of each generated interest transaction record for audit and reconciliation purposes.

variables.name: COB-SS
variables.description: Seconds component of a COBOL-formatted timestamp, used when constructing or parsing the date/time stamp applied to generated interest transactions.

variables.name: COB-MIL
variables.description: Milliseconds (hundredths of a second) component of a COBOL-formatted timestamp, providing sub-second precision on the date/time stamp applied to generated interest transactions.

variables.name: COB-REST
variables.description: Remaining trailing portion of a COBOL-formatted timestamp beyond milliseconds, used to complete the full timestamp structure applied to generated interest transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-FORMAT-TS
variables.description: Full 26-character timestamp formatted in DB2/ISO standard (YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mmmmm), used to date-stamp each interest charge transaction record written to the transaction output file, ensuring a precise and database-compatible audit trail of when charges were generated.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Overlay structure that breaks the DB2-formatted timestamp into its individual date and time components (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond), allowing the program to populate or inspect each part of the transaction timestamp independently when generating interest charge records.

variables.name: DB2-YYYY
variables.description: Four-digit year portion of the DB2 timestamp applied to generated interest transactions, ensuring the billing cycle year is correctly recorded on each charge record.

variables.name: DB2-STREEP-1
variables.description: First separator character (hyphen '-') in the DB2 timestamp format between year and month, required to conform to the DB2/ISO timestamp standard used in transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-MM
variables.description: Two-digit month portion of the DB2 timestamp applied to generated interest transactions, identifying the billing month in which the interest charge was assessed.

variables.name: DB2-STREEP-2
variables.description: Second separator character (hyphen '-') in the DB2 timestamp format between month and day, required to conform to the DB2/ISO timestamp standard used in transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-DD
variables.description: Two-digit day portion of the DB2 timestamp applied to generated interest transactions, recording the exact billing date on which the interest charge was posted.

variables.name: DB2-STREEP-3
variables.description: Third separator character (hyphen '-') in the DB2 timestamp format between date and time portions, required to conform to the DB2/ISO timestamp standard used in transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-HH
variables.description: Two-digit hour portion of the DB2 timestamp applied to generated interest transactions, providing time-of-day precision on the audit record of when the batch interest charge was posted.

variables.name: DB2-DOT-1
variables.description: First dot separator character in the DB2 timestamp time portion (between hours and minutes), required to conform to the DB2/ISO timestamp standard used in transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-MIN
variables.description: Two-digit minutes portion of the DB2 timestamp applied to generated interest transactions, providing minute-level precision on the audit trail of when the interest charge was posted.

variables.name: DB2-DOT-2
variables.description: Second dot separator character in the DB2 timestamp time portion (between minutes and seconds), required to conform to the DB2/ISO timestamp standard used in transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-SS
variables.description: Two-digit seconds portion of the DB2 timestamp applied to generated interest transactions, providing second-level precision on the audit trail of when the interest charge was posted.

variables.name: DB2-DOT-3
variables.description: Third dot separator character in the DB2 timestamp time portion (between seconds and milliseconds), required to conform to the DB2/ISO timestamp standard used in transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-MIL
variables.description: Two-digit milliseconds portion of the DB2 timestamp applied to generated interest transactions, providing sub-second precision on the audit trail timestamp to distinguish closely timed postings within the same batch run.

variables.name: DB2-REST
variables.description: Remaining trailing characters of the DB2 timestamp beyond milliseconds, used to pad or complete the full 26-character DB2/ISO timestamp format required on generated interest transaction records.

variables.name: WS-MISC-VARS
variables.description: Group of miscellaneous working-storage variables that collectively manage the state of the interest calculation process across accounts and transaction categories during the batch run.

variables.name: WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM
variables.description: Remembers the account number that was most recently processed. When the program reads a new transaction category balance record with a different account number, this value triggers the posting of accumulated interest to the previous account's master record before starting fresh calculations for the new account.

variables.name: WS-MONTHLY-INT
variables.description: The interest charge amount calculated for a single transaction category within the current account (e.g., interest on the purchase balance or cash advance balance for one rate tier). This is computed by applying the category-specific interest rate to the outstanding category balance and is then added to the account-level total.

variables.name: WS-TOTAL-INT
variables.description: Running total of all interest charges accumulated across every transaction category for the current account being processed. Once all categories for an account have been evaluated, this total is posted to the account master record as the combined monthly interest charge.

variables.name: WS-FIRST-TIME
variables.description: A flag that prevents the program from attempting to update an account master record before any real account data has been loaded. Set to 'Y' at the start of the batch run, it suppresses the account-update step when the very first transaction category record is encountered, avoiding a spurious or erroneous posting to a blank account.

variables.name: WS-COUNTERS
variables.description: Group of counters used to track batch run statistics and ensure uniqueness of generated records, supporting reconciliation reporting and audit trail integrity.

variables.name: WS-RECORD-COUNT
variables.description: Counts the total number of transaction category balance records read and processed during the batch run. Used in end-of-job reporting to confirm how many account-category combinations were evaluated for interest, supporting reconciliation against the input file.

variables.name: WS-TRANID-SUFFIX
variables.description: A sequential counter incremented each time a new interest or fee transaction record is generated. Combined with other identifying information, it forms a unique transaction ID for each charge posted, ensuring no two system-generated interest transactions share the same identifier within a single batch run.

variables.name: EXTERNAL-PARMS
variables.description: Group structure holding the parameters passed into the batch job at execution time, allowing the interest calculation run to be controlled externally by the job scheduler or operations team.

variables.name: PARM-LENGTH
variables.description: The byte length of the parameter string passed to the batch job at execution time. Used by the program to validate that a processing date parameter was actually supplied before attempting to use it, preventing the job from running with a missing or malformed billing date.

variables.name: PARM-DATE
variables.description: The billing or statement cycle date supplied externally when the batch job is submitted (e.g., '2023-09-30'). This date is used to date-stamp all generated interest charge transactions and determines the period-end date for which monthly interest is being calculated, enabling the job to be run for any specific billing cycle rather than always defaulting to today's date.

paragraphs.name: 0000-TCATBALF-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the Transaction Category Balance file at the start of the batch interest calculation run, making the outstanding balances available for processing. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately halts with an error, preventing any interest calculations from proceeding on incomplete or unavailable data.

paragraphs.name: 0100-XREFFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: Opens the Card-to-Account Cross-Reference file so the batch interest calculation run can resolve card numbers to their corresponding account identifiers. If the file cannot be opened, the program halts immediately to prevent interest charges from being posted against incorrectly identified accounts.

paragraphs.name: 0200-DISCGRP-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the Interest Rate Group file, which holds the applicable interest rates by account group, transaction type, and category. It is a mandatory setup step before any interest calculation can begin; if the file cannot be opened, the entire batch job is halted immediately to prevent incorrect or missing interest postings.

paragraphs.name: 0300-ACCTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: Opens the Account Master file in read/write mode so the batch run can both retrieve existing account data and post computed interest charges back to it. If the file cannot be opened, the program halts immediately to prevent any interest calculations from proceeding against an inaccessible file.

paragraphs.name: 0400-TRANFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the transaction output file that will receive all newly generated interest charge and fee records for the current batch run. It ensures the file is ready to accept writes before any interest calculations begin, and halts the entire batch job immediately if the file cannot be opened.

paragraphs.name: 1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph advances the batch process by reading the next transaction category balance record, which represents an outstanding balance for a specific account, transaction type, and category combination. It handles all possible read outcomes — successful read, end of file, or a file error — ensuring the batch either continues processing, gracefully concludes, or halts safely with a diagnostic message.

paragraphs.name: 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph finalises the account master record at the end of each account's interest calculation cycle by posting the total accumulated interest charges to the account's outstanding balance and resetting the current billing cycle activity counters, then writing the updated record back to the account master file. If the write fails, the program halts immediately to prevent corrupt or incomplete interest postings from propagating downstream.

paragraphs.name: 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the full account master record for the account currently being processed, so that account-level details such as group classification and balances are available for interest calculation. If the account cannot be found or a file error occurs, the batch run is immediately halted to prevent incorrect interest postings.

paragraphs.name: 1110-GET-XREF-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph resolves the account identifier by looking up the card-to-account cross-reference record, ensuring that interest charges are correctly associated with the right customer account. If the account cannot be found or the lookup fails, the program halts immediately to prevent incorrect interest postings.

paragraphs.name: 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the applicable interest rate for the current combination of account group, transaction type, and transaction category from the rate table. If no specific rate record exists for the account's group classification, it falls back to a default rate group to ensure every category receives an interest rate assignment.

paragraphs.name: 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the applicable interest rate record from the discount/rate group table for the current account group, transaction type, and category combination. If the read fails, the program logs the error and halts the batch run to prevent incorrect interest calculations from being posted.

paragraphs.name: 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST
paragraphs.description: This paragraph calculates the monthly interest charge for a single transaction category balance by applying the category-specific annual interest rate, then accumulates the result into the account-level interest total and records the charge as an auditable transaction.

paragraphs.name: 1300-B-WRITE-TX
paragraphs.description: This paragraph constructs and writes a single interest charge transaction record to the transaction output file, creating an auditable record of the monthly interest applied to a specific transaction category on a credit card account. It stamps the transaction with a unique identifier, system-generated metadata, and the calculated interest amount before persisting it, aborting the batch run if the write fails.

paragraphs.name: 1400-COMPUTE-FEES
paragraphs.description: This paragraph is intended to calculate and apply any fees associated with a transaction category balance (such as late fees, annual fees, or penalty charges) as part of the monthly interest and fee posting cycle. It is currently a placeholder and has not yet been implemented.

paragraphs.name: 9000-TCATBALF-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the Transaction Category Balance file after all account interest calculations have been completed for the batch run. It validates that the file closed successfully and halts the entire batch job with an error if the file cannot be closed cleanly, protecting data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9100-XREFFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the Card-to-Account Cross-Reference file once all account lookups for the batch interest run are complete. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program logs the failure and halts immediately to prevent data integrity issues.

paragraphs.name: 9200-DISCGRP-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph closes the Interest Rate Group reference file after all rate lookups have been completed for the batch run. It ensures the file is properly released and halts the entire batch job with a logged error if the file cannot be closed cleanly.

paragraphs.name: 9300-ACCTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the Account Master file at the end of the batch interest calculation run, ensuring all posted interest charges and balance updates are properly flushed and the file is released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program raises a critical error and halts processing to prevent data corruption or incomplete postings.

paragraphs.name: 9400-TRANFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Closes the transaction output file that holds all newly generated interest charge and fee records for the current batch run. Ensures the file is properly sealed and all audit trail records are safely committed to storage before the program ends.

paragraphs.name: Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the current system date and time and formats it into a standardised database timestamp, ensuring that every interest charge transaction record generated during the batch run is stamped with a precise, consistently formatted point-in-time reference suitable for storage and audit retrieval.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs a controlled emergency shutdown of the interest calculation batch job when an unrecoverable error is encountered, ensuring the failure is clearly signalled to the operating environment so that no partial or incorrect interest postings are silently accepted as successful.

paragraphs.name: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and displays a human-readable file error status code whenever a file operation fails during batch interest processing, enabling operations staff to diagnose which file encountered an error and what type of failure occurred. It handles two distinct error encoding formats to ensure the status is always presented in a consistent four-digit display regardless of the underlying error type.
